title: Build the button component in the right order
prompt: You are building Steady's button: Type and State as variant properties, plus a text property for the label, a boolean to show the icon and an instance swap for which icon. Put the steps in the order that avoids redoing work.
hints: A component property can only be created on something that is already a component.
New variants copy the property connections of the component they were created from.
Base frame, component, properties, variants, styling, then test.
explanation: Start with a well-built **auto layout frame** with named Icon and Label layers, because everything after inherits its structure. **Make it a component**, then add the **text, boolean and instance swap properties** while there is only one variant to connect them to. Next **add variants** and name the variant properties Type and State; each new variant inherits those property connections. Then **restyle** each variant for its type and state. Finally **test an instance** by switching every property, including long labels and the icon off, to prove nothing breaks before anyone else uses it.

items.build-base: Build the default primary button as an auto layout frame with named Icon and Label layers.
items.make-component: Turn the frame into a main component.
items.add-props: Add a text property for Label, a boolean for Show icon and an instance swap for Icon.
items.add-variants: Add variants and name the variant properties Type and State with their values.
items.style-variants: Restyle each variant: secondary and ghost colors, pressed and disabled states.
items.test-instance: Place an instance and switch every property, with a long label and the icon off, to check nothing breaks.
